steps: Choose the schools that hold these children now: the lead's lists, or by default the nearest 15 state primaries (at 16+, the nearest 10 state secondaries, 11-16 schools first, plus your own Year 11, with the primaries below).

Counted years: for each September from 2027, find the age those children are now (entry age minus years to go) and add up these schools' pupils at that age in the January 2026 census. That count is the line. At 16+, the move from the primaries to the secondaries is scaled by the average ratio seen between them in past years.

Range for counted years: take every year-on-year change in these schools' year groups since 2019/20 (same schools in both years), keep the middle 80% (10th to 90th percentile), and apply the low and high ends once for each year still to go, so the range widens.

Years beyond the youngest counted age, from births: blend each LA's births by its weight (a weighted average). A school year is 8/12 of calendar year X plus 4/12 of year X-1. Scale this to your schools by the average ratio of their Reception pupils to those births in past years, then follow it forward as in step 4; the range also uses the low and high Reception ratios. For girls or boys, births are taken as 49% or 51%.
At 4+ (and younger entry ages) the blended births are the pool itself, not scaled to the schools; the range is the spread of the Reception-to-births ratio around its average.
